claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years. The Panthers take a lot of penalties, so the Oilers’ power play should get its chances.

story.head: The Oilers come in hot
paras: The Panthers (12-7-3) lost 2-1 in overtime to Dallas on Sunday. The Oilers have won five straight, and they’re rolling. Going in, the Oilers are first in the NHL and the Cats fifth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth in the NHL).
The Oilers’ record (.795) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.559), largely thanks to their finishing. The Panthers’ record (.614) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and their power play against the Panthers’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Edmonton has scored 3.91 goals a game, the third most in the league. On the other side, the Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st), hit a lot (1st) and don’t block many shots (32nd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Connor McDavid (12 G / 41 A / 53 P in 22 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (20 G / 21 A / 41 P in 22 GP) has a team-high 20 goals, the most in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Matthew Tkachuk (5 G / 25 A / 30 P in 22 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL. Sam Reinhart (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with a point in five straight games against Edmonton.
Devon Levi (9-1-0 / .906 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to start for Edmonton, and Jacob Markström (6-3-1 / .905 SV% in 11 GS) for Florida.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Imama, Schwindt and Hathaway out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Formenton, Michaels and Joseph.
